chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) about the major sins, and he said: They are seven in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام): kufr in Allah, killing the soul, disobedience to parents, consuming usury after the clarification, consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, fleeing from the battlefield, and reverting to desert-life after the Hijrah.

He said: So I said, Are these the greatest sins? He said: Yes. I said: Is consuming one dirham from the wealth of an orphan unjustly graver, or abandoning the salat (prayer)? He said: Abandoning the salat (prayer). I said: Then you did not count abandoning the salat (prayer) among the major sins? So he said: What was the first thing I said to you? He said: I said: Kufr. He said: Indeed, the one who abandons the salat (prayer) is a kāfir, meaning without an excuse.

key_terms.التَّعَرُّبُ بَعْدَ الْهِجْرَةِ: reverting to uncultured desert-life after migration to the Islamic community
key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury, the forbidden gain from interest-based increase
key_terms.الزَّحْفِ: the battlefield or advancing battle line
key_terms.الْكُفْرُ: disbelief in Allah; the first and greatest sin mentioned
key_terms.عُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ: disobedience and undutiful conduct toward one's parents
key_terms.مَالِ الْيَتِيمِ: the property of the orphan, whose wrongful consumption is a grave sin

ai.seo_question: What are the major sins in al-Kāfī, and why is abandoning salat (prayer) considered so grave?
ai.summary: This hadith lists seven major sins recorded in the Book of ʿAlī (عليه السلام), including kufr, killing unjustly, disobedience to parents, usury, and consuming an orphan's wealth. It further teaches that abandoning salat (prayer) without a valid excuse is even graver and is described here as kufr, underscoring the centrality of salat (prayer) in Islam.
